insights.headline: Deutsche Bank flags silver surplus by 2027; gold steadies as October Fed hike bets fade
insights.summary: Deutsche Bank says silver's years-long physical shortage could flip to a surplus as early as 2027, with London vault stocks ample and solar demand fading; it expects spot silver to average $70/oz by Q2 2027. September's weak US jobs report crushed the odds of an October Fed rate hike from near 70% to about 18%, but gold steadied near $4,135 as a firm dollar and elevated yields capped gains. In India, MCX gold slipped about 1% while silver held firmer, and the GST Council is set to consider withdrawing the IGST exemption on gold and silver imports by banks and nominated agencies on October 7.
points: Deutsche Bank: London's freely available silver stockpile up 70% since Oct 2025; solar silver use per cell down 17% in 2026.
US payrolls rose just 29,000 in September vs 90,000 expected; October Fed hike odds fell to ~18%, unemployment at 4.2%.
MCX gold fell ~1% to ₹1,49,150/10g on Monday while silver edged up ₹173 to ₹2,26,050/kg, PL Capital's Ashish Rajodiya notes.
GST Council may withdraw the 2017 IGST exemption on gold, silver and platinum imports by banks and nominated agencies on Oct 7.
India's silver imports running 25% below year-ago levels after higher duties; Deutsche says inventories can cover festive buying.

trending.title: Silver's deficit era may be ending
trending.summary: Deutsche Bank says a 2027 silver surplus is possible as London stocks swell and solar demand thrifts. India's silver imports lag 25% behind last year, though inventories should cover festive demand.

trending.title: Fed expectations keep flipping
trending.summary: Weak jobs data crushed October hike odds to ~18% from ~70%, lifting gold — yet a firm dollar and elevated yields keep capping the metal's upside.

trending.title: Policy risk on the import channel
trending.summary: The GST Council is expected to weigh withdrawing the IGST exemption on gold, silver and platinum imports by banks and nominated agencies on October 7.

trending.title: Festive season meets record prices
trending.summary: With gold near ₹1.5 lakh per 10g in India's first 15%-duty festive season, jewellers expect strong buying on lighter designs, while jewellery stocks are glittering.

items.title: Silver shortage could flip to surplus in 2027: Deutsche
items.summary: Deutsche Bank says silver's physical shortage could flip to surplus as early as 2027 on rising inventories and weaker industrial demand. London's freely available vault supply is up 70% since October 2025, while solar makers cut silver use via thinner contacts and cheaper pastes, metals head Daniel Ghali notes. He expects spot silver to average $70/oz by Q2 2027, below first-half 2026 levels.

items.title: Gold gains as October Fed rate hike prospects fade
items.summary: Spot gold rose 0.4% to $4,158 an ounce on Monday after September’s weak US jobs report slashed October Fed hike expectations. Payrolls rose just 29,000 against 90,000 expected, with prior months revised down; markets now see a 22% chance of an October hike, down from 64% a week ago. Silver gained 1.7% to $61.40.

items.title: Gold falls nearly 1%, silver gains on MCX: What is driving bullion prices
items.summary: MCX gold futures slipped about 1% — ₹1,020 per 10g — to ₹1.49 lakh as the US dollar climbed to an 18-month high of 102.37 and Treasury yields stayed elevated, while silver rose 0.54% (₹1,223/kg) to ₹2.27 lakh per kg; international spot gold held steady near $4,163.50 an ounce.

items.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD builds base above $60, eyes $64
items.summary: Silver (XAG/USD) rose over 1% to $61.13 on Monday despite rising US Treasury yields and a stronger dollar, FXStreet's technical analysis notes. Price action suggests a bottom may be forming above $60, with a likely test of resistance above $64; a move past $62 could bring the 50- and 100-day averages into play. A break below the October 2 low of $59.69 would risk a deeper reversal.

items.title: GST exemption for banks, nominated agencies for gold, silver imports may be withdrawn
items.summary: The GST Council is likely to consider withdrawing the 3% IGST exemption on gold, silver and platinum imports by banks and nominated agencies at its Oct 7 meeting, sources said. The relief dates to 2017, when bullion trade was tightly canalised; scrapping it would put banks, nominated agencies and bullion exchanges on the same tax footing, after import duty was hiked to 15% in May.

items.title: Gold struggles as dovish Fed repricing meets stronger US Dollar, elevated yields
items.summary: Spot gold traded around $4,158, up 0.35%, caught between receding October Fed hike bets — weak September payrolls (29K vs 90K expected) cut October hike odds to about 20% — and a dollar index at 102.53, its highest since April 2025, plus a 10-year US yield near 5.29%. Deutsche Bank still sees two more 25bp hikes; FXStreet's chart view puts resistance at $4,200 and support at $4,100.

items.title: RBI likely intervenes to support rupee, traders say
items.summary: The rupee held at 96.24 to the dollar on Monday as state-run banks were seen selling dollars, most likely on behalf of the RBI, four traders told Reuters. The move helped the currency withstand a broadly stronger dollar - the dollar index hit a more than one-year high of 102.5 - and volatile oil prices. A weaker rupee keeps imported gold and silver costlier for Indian buyers.

items.title: Gold retains key reserve status despite surging bond yields, central bankers say
items.summary: Bank of Italy deputy governor Altimari told the LBMA's Sorrento conference gold remains "probably the safe haven asset", flagging a structural shift since 2022 from emerging-economy central-bank buying. Bundesbank chief Nagel said the case for gold diversification stands despite rising yields; Metals Focus sees 2026 central-bank demand easing 15% to 720 tonnes, still above pre-2022 levels.

items.title: Bullion faces choppy week as dollar, US-Iran risks test sentiment: Analysts
items.summary: Analysts expect gold and silver to stay turbulent next week as a strong dollar and high Treasury yields clash with unresolved US-Iran tensions; the RBI's rate decision on Wednesday is the other key cue. Last week MCX gold fell about 2% to ₹1.5 lakh per 10 grams and silver about 4% to ₹2.25 lakh per kg; Comex gold dropped 3.7% to $4,162.3 an ounce.

items.title: Silver Gains as Fed Rate Hike Bets Ease
items.summary: Silver climbed above $61 an ounce on Monday as weak US September jobs data eased pressure on the Fed to raise rates further. Payrolls rose just 29,000 against 90,000 expected, unemployment edged up to 4.2% and wage growth slowed to 3.0%, its weakest since May 2021. Markets now price about a 20% chance of an October hike.

items.title: Risks for $1 trillion-a-week gold market as rule-setter LBMA fights for survival
items.summary: The LBMA, which sets the rules for London's $1 trillion-a-week gold market, is fighting a London court case that insiders fear could leave it insolvent, investingLive reports. At stake are the Good Delivery List and the responsible-sourcing regime underpinning global bullion trade. The report lands as the market debates the long-term survival of the gold market's key rule-setter.

items.title: Titan, Kalyan Jewellers, PC Jeweller shares shine - Why jewellery stocks are glittering? Expert decodes rally
items.summary: Shares of Indian jewellery retailers rallied on Monday on hopes of strong festive-season sales. Kalyan Jewellers led with a 4.5% gain while Titan and PC Jeweller rose about 1.5%. Bonanza analyst Abhinav Tiwari said the market is positioning ahead of Dhanteras and Diwali, though the move is largely expectation-driven before September-quarter sales updates.

items.title: Gold Nears ₹1.5 Lakh per 10 Grams as India Heads into Its First 15% Duty Dhanteras
items.summary: At ~₹1.49 lakh per 10 grams this is the most expensive Dhanteras on record, and the first under the 15% import duty. The premium decomposes neatly: $4,140/oz at a rupee near 96.3 gives ~₹1.28 lakh landed parity, and 15% duty plus 3% GST add most of the rest. WGC Q2 data: jewellery volumes fell 15.4% while bars and coins rose 8.9%; loans against gold jewellery surged 83% to ₹5.6 lakh crore.

items.title: Festive season outlook: Jewellers expect strong buying despite changing consumer patterns
items.summary: CNBC-TV18 reports jewellers expect strong festive and wedding-season buying even as high gold prices change how consumers buy: lighter, lower-carat, versatile pieces within defined budgets, traction for old-gold exchange, and more room for diamonds. WGC: Q2 jewellery demand fell 15% YoY to 75 tonnes while value rose 34%; CRISIL sees 20–25% revenue growth for organised retailers this fiscal.

items.title: Gold, silver lose lustre in September
items.summary: Both precious metals posted negative September returns as a stronger dollar and US rate-hike expectations dented sentiment: Comex gold fell 6.8% to $4,189.1 an ounce and Comex silver 9.6% to $60.75. On MCX, gold dropped 4.1% to Rs 1,49,092 per 10 grams and silver 6.8% to Rs 2,23,740 per kg - the rupee's weakness against the dollar softening the domestic fall.
